\toprule
Existing file & Relevant declarations or interface & Reuse here\\
\midrule\endhead
\path{SignSequence.lean} &
\code{SignSequence}, \code{birthday}, \code{birthdays\_bounded},
\code{small\_bounded}, \code{not\_small} &
Carrier, numerical order, bounded birthday stages, and properness relative
to a universe.\\[5pt]
\path{SignSequenceCut.lean} &
\code{small\_cut\_fillers},
{\small\path{exists_cut_separator_of_birthday_lt}} &
Small-cut realization and prescribed upper birthday control.\\[5pt]
\path{SignSequenceCutOperation.lean} &
\code{cut}, \code{cut\_realizes}, \code{birthday\_cut\_le\_iSup},
\code{exists\_separator\_of\_small\_sets} &
Canonical separators with explicit smallness assumptions.\\[5pt]
\path{SignSequenceSimplicity.lean} &
\code{existsUnique\_simplest\_separator} and minimum-birthday results &
Deterministic choices and control of sign-prefix cuts.\\[5pt]
\path{SizeObstructions.lean} &
\code{SmallCutData}, \code{noUnrestrictedCuts} &
Keep small inputs distinct from an unrestricted self-cut.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

All paths in the table lie below
\path{Algebra/SurrealNumbers/Surreal/Foundations/}; the pinned sources
are recorded in the bibliography \cite{ProveItSigns,ProveItCutFill,ProveItCuts,ProveItSize}.
No Lean build was performed for this article, and no proposed module name
below should be read as an existing theorem declaration.

\subsubsection{Two formalization routes}

The most economical first route is ordinary type-theoretic order theory.
Use a bounded birthday carrier known to be small, transport it with
\code{Shrink} if convenient, and prove the set-alphabet theorems. Store
the numerical label order separately from the well-order being encoded.
A proposed \code{WellOrderOn X} can store the binary relation, strict
linearity, and \code{WellFounded} evidence; an enumeration stores an
ordinal domain with a bijection to $X$. Prove the relation/enumeration
correspondence, prefix-incomparability, and first-disagreement comparison
before taking any quotient. Quotienting first by abstract isomorphism
would destroy the required labels.

The second route explicitly formalizes a model of class theory. Introduce
separate carriers of set and admitted-class codes, membership, formula
semantics, and internally admitted family relations. State elementary
comprehension, replacement, and any GC or ETR assumptions at that level.
This route is appropriate for exact axiom-strength claims and Henkin
models. It is heavier than proving the bounded combinatorial theorems, but
it prevents an accidental use of all ambient predicates as internal classes.

\subsubsection{Universe levels and logical levels are different}

ProveIt's actual carrier is
\[
 \code{SignSequence.\{u\}}:\code{Type (u + 1)},
 \qquad \code{birthday}:\code{Ordinal.\{u\}}.
\]
Its small-cut interfaces explicitly require \code{Small.\{u\}} for the
index families. A bounded birthday subtype is small at that level, while
the full sign carrier is not.

One must not say that every power set automatically forces the next
syntactic Lean universe. If $S:\code{Type (u + 1)}$, then both
\code{Set S} and \code{S -> S -> Prop} also inhabit
\code{Type (u + 1)}. Being well-typed does not make them
\code{u}-small, nor does it identify them with the class collection of
an internal GBC model. Native quantification over all such predicates
is an ambient full-type interpretation. Likewise, native
\code{WellFounded R} asserts ambient well-foundedness, which is not
automatically a model's internal assertion
\cite{LeanUniverses,MathlibSet,MathlibOrdinal}.

For a direct universe-relative global development, keep a baseline
$b:\Ord^{u}\simeq\No^{u}$ as an explicit parameter until its existence
is separately established. Encode supported permutations by genuinely
small data, and represent families of their evaluated graphs uniformly.
This gives meaningful theorems without pretending that every ambient
type is an internal set or every function on class predicates is a
same-level class function.

\subsubsection{Suggested milestones}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Finite and set-alphabet layer.} Formalize first disagreement,
prefix convexity, pair coding, and the stabilization bound. This isolates
the ordinal-spectrum theorem from all surreal-specific facts.
\item \textbf{Topological layer.} Formalize the no-cross-fiber-jump lemma,
prefix families meeting every open set, and disjoint finite-tail
cylinders. Then prove the countable incompleteness construction and the
regular-stage gap spectrum.
\item \textbf{Small-support layer.} Formalize normalization, completion
of a small prefix, and the bounded common-prefix interpolation search.
Reuse the existing small-cut separator rather than postulating a new
unrestricted cut operation.
\item \textbf{Cut recognition.} Define straddling on set codes, prove
uniqueness and coherence at each length, and implement the direct
formula \eqref{swo:ds:eq:recognitionformula}. Only then package the exhaustive
branch criterion and first-failure classification.
\item \textbf{Class semantics layer.} In an explicit model interface,
formalize set-interval equivalence, least representatives, local rank,
and the terminal set. These are elementary constructions; a general
class-recursion engine is unnecessary for them.
\item \textbf{Higher comprehension.} State the inverse evaluator with
its exact syntactic complexity before invoking a comprehension axiom.
Prove the elementary diagonal theorem independently, and use it as the
final contradiction in the nonembedding theorem.
\end{enumerate}

These milestones deliberately separate ordinary mathematics about a large
type from metatheorems about a two-sorted model. No new consistency axiom
is needed for the bounded results, and the inaccessible model is an
optional explicit interpretation rather than a prerequisite for the
whole subject.

% ---- source 17 (batch-81 manuscript 05), lines 1609-1714
\subsection{Source 17: formalization routes and a practical verification plan}
\label{swo:gs:sec:formalization}

\subsubsection{Start with the alphabet interface, not surreal arithmetic}
The new set-sized results depend on a small interface. A formal development
can begin with a linear order $X$ of infinite cardinality $\mu$, with
$\mu$ elements in every nonempty open interval and ray. It should record
its ray and point character $r$ and the gap spectra of deletions of fewer
than $\mu$ elements. Prefix completion, clopen cylinders, divergence
bounds, the cut trichotomy, and fusion can then be proved abstractly.
The birthday sign alphabet is one implementation of this interface.
This organization prevents arithmetic lemmas about surreal addition or
multiplication from obscuring a proof that uses only order and signs.

The exact gap theorem has four independently testable mathematical
interfaces: a gap is a two-sided partition without endpoints; a
straddling prefix is a set witness; the first stopping stage is a
successor, a proper limit, or full length; and each resulting character
is computed separately. Separating them makes it difficult to accidentally
substitute point character $q$ for cylinder character $r$.

The support theorem is another independent target. Its statement needs
only a set partial injection, the necessarily moved domain and range,
cardinal addition, and a complement bijection. No surreal construction
appears until the final composition with a baseline.

\subsubsection{Proposed modules and proof obligations}
The following names describe a proposed architecture, not files claimed
to exist in the repository or in this package.
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}p{.37\textwidth}Y@{}}\toprule
Proposed module & Principal obligation\\\midrule
\path{WellOrders/CommonPrefix.lean} & Elementary predecessor formula,
maximality, first residual labels, transitivity\\[3pt]
\path{WellOrders/PartialSupport.lean} & Mandatory support, deficiency
balance, exact reserve cardinal and extension\\[3pt]
\path{WellOrders/PrefixTopology.lean} & Completion, convex clopen cylinders,
point versus cylinder character, base cardinality\\[3pt]
\path{WellOrders/CutTrichotomy.lean} & Unique straddling path, first failure,
limit boundary, nonexhaustive branch\\[3pt]
\path{Surreal/CutoffGapSpectrum.lean} & Sign-path classification of alphabet
gaps and stability under small deletion\\[3pt]
\path{WellOrders/Fusion.lean} & Dense-open refinement with explicit coverage
of the alphabet\\[3pt]
\path{ClassOrders/BranchRecognition.lean} & A chosen model or size interface;
elementary reconstruction from unique set witnesses\\[3pt]
\path{ClassOrders/CoreAutomorphisms.lean} & Represented-cut preservation,
uniqueness of extension, nonextension witness\\\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

For the topology modules, one should formalize the definition of
cellularity as a supremum before claiming an exact cardinal value. A
supremum of disjoint-family sizes need not be attained. Likewise the gap
spectrum should not include point cuts of character $1$, and the
recognition module should not quietly switch between open and closed
principal lower cuts.

\subsubsection{Universe-relative type theory}
Lean's universes offer a practical way to keep a fixed smaller universe
separate from a larger carrier. A type, a type of relations on it, and a
universe of all smaller types must have their levels checked explicitly.
Function types do not automatically jump one level merely because they
represent a mathematically large collection: their levels are computed
from the domain and codomain. Universe polymorphism supplies a family of
declarations, not an internal type of all universes; and universe lifting
is explicit rather than an automatic cumulative coercion
\cite{LeanUniverses}.

For this project, choose a lower notion of ``small'' and an ordinal index
which well-orders the intended large carrier with small proper initial
segments. State the cut operation only for lower-small families. A
back-and-forth argument along an arbitrary choice well-order of the large
type is unsafe: its proper initial segments may be too large for the
assumed cut operation. The correct interface is the small-history property
used in the proof of \Cref{swo:gs:cor:core-isomorphism}.

A set-sized cutoff implementation avoids this difficulty entirely. Every
object is an ordinary type with explicit cardinal bounds, and a formal
proof can be instantiated at many cardinals. A universe-relative version
then transports the argument, without equating an ordinal type from one
universe with all ordinals from every universe.

\subsubsection{A deep model-theoretic alternative}
To study exactly which comprehension principles suffice, formalize a
specified two-sorted model $(M,\mathcal X)$ and its elementary
comprehension and replacement axioms. Each theorem about global rows is
then a theorem about admissible class relations of that model. This is
the most direct route for \Cref{swo:gs:thm:class-extension} and for
questions comparing $\GBC$, $\ETR$, and $\KM$.

The two routes should not be conflated. A successful theorem about types
in a fixed universe does not, without an interpretation theorem, prove a
conservativity or axiomatic-strength statement about class theory.
Conversely, a GBC proof with explicit class variables is not automatically
a compiled theorem about the repository's current sign-sequence carrier.

\subsubsection{Verification boundary}
No Lean code accompanies this article and no kernel-verification claim is
made. The source's foundation modules were not rebuilt. A future
formalization should pin both the repository and Mathlib revisions,
compile the modules, reject unfinished proofs, and audit theorem axiom
dependencies. The companion Python checks test only finite mechanisms.
They cannot decide the existence of class maps, prove cardinal cofinality
formulas, or certify the infinite support obstruction.

\subsection{Source 18: a concrete formalization plan for ProveIt}
\label{swo:sh:sec:formalization}

\subsubsection{What the inspected source actually provides}

The source audit used the pinned revision
\texttt{83befe707f2840c2b53e0606701d8a2b28598e47}.
The relevant files are in
\path{Algebra/SurrealNumbers/Surreal/Foundations/}.
The following declarations were inspected directly in the source
files \cite{ProveItFoundationsDir}, rather than inferred from a report's title.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.31\textwidth}Y@{}}
\toprule
Source file & Useful declarations and their role\\
\midrule
\texttt{SignSequence.lean} &
\texttt{SignSequence : Type (u + 1)}, numerical linear order,
\texttt{lt\_iff}, \texttt{birthdays\_bounded},
\texttt{small\_bounded}, \texttt{not\_small},
prefixes, truncations, and the ordinal order embedding\\[3pt]
\texttt{SignSequenceCut.lean} &
\texttt{exists\_cut\_separator\_of\_birthday\_lt} and
\texttt{small\_cut\_fillers}; the bounded and small-family separator
interface\\[3pt]
\texttt{SignSequenceSimplicity.lean} &
\texttt{existsUnique\_simplest\_separator} and minimum-birthday
uniqueness; deterministic choice of separators where appropriate\\[3pt]
\texttt{SignSequenceComparison.lean} &
\texttt{le\_iff\_options\_lt},
\texttt{lt\_iff\_exists\_option}, and canonical-cut comparison\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

The declaration $\texttt{SignSequence.\{u\}}$ living in
$\texttt{Type (u+1)}$ is crucial. It contains the surreals with
$u$-small birthdays; the theorem \texttt{not\_small} says that this
whole type is not itself $u$-small. The existence of a Lean type is
therefore not the same as being a set at the intended smaller size
level. Lean's universe hierarchy enforces these distinctions
\cite{LeanUniverses}. A Tarski--Grothendieck implementation is another
well-developed option; P\k{a}k and Kaliszyk's Mizar formalization
illustrates a concrete universe-based route \cite{PakKaliszyk}.

This article does not assert that the new spectrum, condensation, or
shuffle theorems are already formalized in these files. No Lean build
or complete imported-axiom audit was performed for this article.
Reading a proof file is not equivalent to running its elaborator and
kernel in the pinned environment.

\subsubsection{The first set-level modules}

The most reusable initial target is independent of surreal arithmetic.
Represent a labelled well-order by a relation on a fixed carrier and
its well-order proof, or by a bijection from an ordinal domain. Prove
the equivalence of these representations and the absence of proper
prefixes for exhaustive enumerations. Keep ``increasing by numerical
order'' as an extra predicate on words, not as part of the definition
of a well-order code.

The suggested sequence is:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Ordinal words.} First disagreement, concatenation,
prefix cones, alternative terminators, and the finite permutation
adjacency criterion.
\item \textbf{Set spectra.} Pair coding, eventual coordinate
stabilization, and the $\mu^+$ obstruction. The central induction is
on a regular successor cardinal, with the domain and range
cardinalities stated separately.
\item \textbf{Permutation topology.} Order topology, dense sets,
disjoint interval families, $Q_n(X)$, and the density/cellularity
transition. Include global endpoints in dense-set constructions for
arbitrary alphabets.
\item \textbf{Surreal cutoff interface.} Large sign cones, preservation
of cut characters after deleting fewer than $\mu$ labels, and
$\cf(2^{<\kappa})\ge\cf\kappa$.
\item \textbf{Cut classification.} Encode the chain of straddling
prefixes and prove its three cases. The multiplicity theorem then
uses explicit injections and the cardinalities of the prefix tree
and full branch set.
\end{enumerate}

This order gives a checkable sequence of finite dependency boundaries.
The proof of the gap spectrum depends only on order, ordinal words,
cardinal arithmetic, and the cutoff interface. It does not require
surreal addition, multiplication, or real closedness.

\subsubsection{The class-level modules}

There are two sensible implementations.

\emph{Semantic set/class models.} Define a first-order set universe
and a collection of admitted class predicates, with the GB axioms
made explicit. A class well-order is a relation in that collection
with the internal well-order property. Then prove the elementary
common-prefix theorem, set-interval decomposition, uniform branch
criterion, and factorial-block facts as statements about that model.
An external countability hypothesis subsequently gives the shuffle
classification. This route preserves the exact meaning of internal
set size and available classes.

\emph{Universe-relative carriers.} Fix the smallness level $u$, work
with a larger carrier type, and formulate set-likeness using
$u$-small predecessor types. Relations on that carrier live in an
appropriate larger universe. This is convenient for a concrete
containing-universe development, but theorems must say which subsets
are admitted and which smallness level ``set'' means. Merely forming
the type of all relations in the next universe does not identify it
with a particular GBC class realization.

In either route, give quotient blocks actual representatives. For
set-interval condensation use the least label of a block; for the
external finite-condensation quotient use the usual set quotient in
the ambient universe. Their types and their purposes differ.

\subsubsection{Suggested proof obligations and trust reporting}

For a mechanized milestone, require the following explicit outputs:
the precise theorem statement with universe levels; a compiling source
file against the pinned toolchain; an imported-axiom report; and a
short explanation of the semantic correspondence with the article.
Finite examples can test a comparator implementation, but they do
not verify the $\mu^+$ argument, Global Choice equivalence, or any
claim about proper classes. The current deliverable supplies
conventional proofs and source provenance, rather than presenting
finite computations as certificates for infinitary assertions.

\section{What this Part answers}\label{swo:ix:sec:status}

embedding and nonembedding theorems between those subpredicates and the
set-like order, of which only the full-model separation
$\WO_{\kappa+2}\not\emb\WO_\kappa$ (\cref{swo:ds:thm:externalnonembedding}) is
proved.
\item \emph{Source~11's \cref{swo:n16.2}, weakest comprehension for the uniform
nonembedding}: answered in part. For transformations defined by formulas with
only set quantifiers, $\GBC$ with $\Sigma^1_1$ class comprehension suffices
(\cref{swo:ds:thm:sigma}); whether it is necessary, and whether $\GBC$ alone
suffices, is open (\cref{swo:ds:n16.6}). The question's bounded variant,
comparing density and cellularity of all well-orders of $\No_{<\kappa}$ with
the minimal stratum, is answered by \cref{swo:ds:thm:density} (Part~VI).
\item \emph{Source~08's question~7, full virtual lexicographic products}
(\cref{swo:sk:sec:research}): \textbf{answered} for the interpretations it
names. In $\GBC$, $\Hsl\cong\No\times_\lex\Hsl$ and every ordinary class-indexed
lexicographic sum of copies of $\Hsl$ embeds into $\Hsl$
(\cref{swo:fs:thm:absorption}); in the full inaccessible universe
$\Hsl\times_\lex2\not\emb\Hsl$, hence $\Hsl\times_\lex\Hsl\not\emb\Hsl$
(\cref{swo:fs:thm:fullsplit}); no fixed definable uniform embedding exists in
$\KM+\GC$ (\cref{swo:fs:thm:kmsplit}); in externally countable models
$\Hsl\times_\lex\Hsl\cong\Hsl$ externally (\cref{swo:fs:prop:countable}). The
negative half already followed from the proofs of
\cref{swo:thm:universe-nonembedding,swo:thm:km-nonembedding}
(\cref{swo:ix:note:products}). A finer absorption spectrum (source~13's
\cref{swo:fs:n15.6}) is open.
\item \emph{Source~12's \cref{swo:st:n14.7}, automorphisms and finite
condensation}: answered in part. The maximal finite components of the
unrestricted order are the $n!$ permutations of the maximal finite final
segment, and the condensed order is dense without endpoints
(\cref{swo:gs:thm:condensation}, \cref{swo:sh:prop:factorial-blocks}); in every
countable $\omega$-standard model the full order is externally the factorial
shuffle and its automorphism orbits are known
(\cref{swo:sh:thm:countable-factorial-shuffle}, \cref{swo:sh:n16.9}). The
internal classification of the condensed order (source~17's
\cref{swo:gs:n15.9}) is open.

source~08's question~12, class realizations}: answered further. In addition to

well-orders is the same factorial shuffle in every countable $\omega$-standard
model, so it records nothing about the class realization there, and

(\cref{swo:sh:thm:countable-factorial-shuffle,swo:sh:cor:setlike-not-order-definable});
among $\GBC$ realizations with the same sets, internal well-foundedness of a
shared relation never changes (\cref{swo:ix:note:wellfounded}). The expanded
structures with the set-like predicate or the label evaluation are open
(\cref{swo:sh:n19.7}).
\item \emph{Source~11's \cref{swo:n16.4}, recovering prefix structure from the
bare order}: a further negative part. Set-likeness is not first-order
definable, even with finitely many parameters, from the pure order of all
admitted class well-orders of a countable $\omega$-standard model
(\cref{swo:sh:cor:setlike-not-order-definable}); within one class well-order
it is recognized by the number of blocks (source~15: $W$ is set-like exactly
when it has one block). With \cref{swo:viii:sec:status}~(c), the question's
negative half is settled; the positive question, which extra predicates
suffice, stays open.

source~09's direction~2, source~08's question~10): bear. The direct comparison,
the block decomposition, the represented-cut reconstruction and the uniform
removal of blocks all have elementary definitions in $\GB$ or $\GBC$ (sources~15,

\item \emph{Source~11's \cref{swo:n16.10}, source~09's direction~9 and
source~08's question~15 (Kanovei--Shelah)}: not affected; sources~14 and~17

\subsection{Source 11's research questions and topics}\label{swo:sec:research}

The questions below are proposed extensions of the present
development. Except where a source is explicitly named, they
are not asserted to be established open problems in the
literature. Several ask for a stronger classification than
the proved results supply.

\subsubsection{A precise description of the represented cuts}

Fix the dense ordinary class \(\Pbd\cong\No\). Every
set-like global enumeration determines a lower cut of
\(\Pbd\), and so does every injective nonexhaustive
\(\Ord\)-word. The omitted-range example shows that the
first collection does not fill every cut generated by the
second.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.1}
Characterize, using the prefix tree and its numerical
labels, exactly which class cuts of \(\Pbd\) arise from
injective \(\Ord\)-words, and which of these words are
exhaustive.
\end{question}

A useful first target is a necessary-and-sufficient
compatibility condition on the intersections of a cut with
prefix cylinders. The challenge is to separate missing
labels, impossible repeated labels, and cuts that escape
every coherent branch. This should first be stated for a
fixed uniform class cut, before quantifying over an entire
hyperclass of cuts.

\subsubsection{The embedding relationship between the two global orders}

The set-like fragment and binary class words are
equimorphic, while the unrestricted order has additional
convex fibers. Theorem~\ref{swo:thm:universe-nonembedding}
rules out a reverse embedding in the full universe
interpretation. Theorem~\ref{swo:thm:km-nonembedding} also
rules out a definable uniform reverse embedding in
\(\KM+\GC\).

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.2}
What is the weakest comprehension scheme over \(\GBC\)
that proves the uniform nonembedding result? Can the
inverse-evaluation step be replaced by an elementary
argument, or is a genuine strengthening necessary?
\end{question}

A precise project should specify the syntactic complexity
of the proposed transformation and of the comprehension
used to invert its code assignment. In the bounded
setting one can instead compare the density and
cellularity of all well-orders of \(\No_{<\kappa}\)
with their minimum-length stratum, especially when
\(\kappa\) is not inaccessible. The full-universe case
is already settled above; the remaining questions
concern strength and wider hypotheses.

\subsubsection{Iterated residual decomposition}

One extraction of the canonical initial \(\Ord\)-part
requires only elementary class comprehension. A residual
proper class has another such part, suggesting a hierarchy
of successive blocks.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.3}
What is the exact recursion strength needed to organize
iterated residual decompositions uniformly, and what
class order types can occur as their block-index orders?
\end{question}

An initial project could analyze finitely many blocks and
specified set-length constructions, recording where the
recursion state becomes a class. The general case should
be compared with known \(\ETR\) results on class
well-order comparability, rather than assumed to follow
from the one-step theorem.

\subsubsection{Recovering the prefix structure from the bare order}

The definitions exhibit a labeled tree of prefixes.
An automorphism of the bare lexicographic order need not
obviously preserve its displayed labels or cylinders.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.4}
Which prefix cones, canonical-core fibers, and finite
permutation blocks are definable from the linear order
alone? What extra predicates make the reconstruction
unique?
\end{question}

Adjacency directly detects finite stretches, but a
singleton fiber can be exhaustive or can omit one label.
Thus local block size alone cannot recover set-likeness.
An analysis of the automorphism group may clarify what
the order remembers about the original enumeration.

\subsubsection{The bounded-support choice of baseline}

Every baseline enumeration gives an ordinary class
\(\Pbd\) abstractly isomorphic to \(\No\). If two
baselines differ on a proper class of positions, their
bounded-support subfamilies can be disjoint.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.5}
How do the two dense classes sit inside the same
\(\Hsl(\No)\), and when does an automorphism of that
higher-order order carry one onto the other?
\end{question}

The abstract isomorphism of the two dense orders does
not automatically extend to all global enumerations.
The represented-cut problem is likely relevant. A
restricted first case is a baseline change obtained by
an order automorphism of the numerical surreal line.

\subsubsection{Sharper birthday bounds and minimal codes}

The explicit code gives a usable bound
\[
 \bd(E(f))=\sum_{i<\dom f}
              \bigl(1+2\cdot\bd(f(i))+2\bigr).
\]
It is designed for a transparent proof, not asserted
to be optimal.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.6}
Which birthday bounds are optimal for uniform embeddings
of injective surreal words? Can shorter prefix-free
coefficient codes preserve useful simplicity relations?
\end{question}

Regular cutoffs permit same-stage compression; singular
cutoffs show why a cardinal bound alone is insufficient.
A sharpened result should specify whether it preserves
only numerical order, prefix extension, simplicity, or
all of these.

\subsubsection{Saturation of more general bounded alphabets}

If \(X\) is an \(\eta_\kappa\) order of cardinality
\(\kappa\), its minimal-length permutation order inherits
\(\eta_\kappa\). Birthday fragments often have cardinality
\(2^{<\kappa}\), which may exceed \(\kappa\).

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.7}
Determine the exact cut spectrum and point characters of
\(\WO_\lambda(\No_{<\kappa})\), where
\(\lambda=2^{<\kappa}\), without assuming
\(2^{<\kappa}=\kappa\).
\end{question}

The issue combines the size of a used prefix with the
number and birthdays of possible numerical separators.
The real-alphabet formulas in the precursor report
cannot settle this case by substitution.

\subsubsection{Class extensions and available global orders}

Two models may have the same sets and hence the same
individual surreal numbers, but different available
classes and different global well-orders.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.8}
Which features of the lexicographic theory are invariant
under extensions of the class part, and how does the
represented-cut collection change?
\end{question}

Uniform formulas such as first divergence remain the
same for the existing relations. Existence of additional
enumerations changes the larger totality. This offers a
way to distinguish properties of the labeled surreal
order from properties of the surrounding class theory.

\subsubsection{A verified first milestone for ProveIt}

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.9}
Can the explicit word compression and the direct
predecessor comparison be formalized first, with a small,
reusable interface independent of surreal arithmetic?
\end{question}

These are concrete, finite-dependency targets:
ordinal concatenation, numerical first difference,
injectivity, and well-order predecessor sets. The next
milestone is the general successor-cardinal obstruction,
followed by bounded-support completion and the
small-family interpolation theorem. This ordering keeps
the central algorithms separate from a formalization of
an entire higher-order set theory.

\subsubsection{Uniform mathematical constructions indexed by well-orders}

The Kanovei--Shelah method suggests using a definable
linear order of codes to index constructions without
selecting one privileged code. The surreal setting
raises additional smallness conditions.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.10}
Which finite-support or bounded-support constructions
can be indexed by a uniform class family of global
well-orders, and which require a genuine higher-order
index object?
\end{question}

A first investigation should specify its support sets,
evaluation maps, and quantifier domains before adding
algebra or model theory. The diagonal theorem prevents
an exhaustive class-code shortcut, but leaves many
useful uniform families available.

\subsection{Source 12's research questions and prioritized program}
\label{swo:st:sec:questions}

The following are proposed continuations. Except where an older question
is explicitly attributed, they are not claimed to be recognized open
problems in the literature.

\begin{question}[All fixed enumeration types]\label{swo:st:n14.1}
Determine $\bl(\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa}))$ for every ordinal $\alpha$ of
cardinality $2^{<\kappa}$, not only the minimal type. Can the answer be
expressed by a precise ordinal-sum invariant of admissible entry-code
lengths, together with the finite terminal permutation factor?
\end{question}
The singular theorem identifies the first obstruction that any such
formula must capture. A useful initial target is
$\alpha=\mu\cdot2$ and then $\mu\cdot\gamma+n$ for finite $n$.

\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday bounds]\label{swo:st:n14.2}
For an arbitrary infinite ordinal $\theta$, classify the minimal
permutation order of $\No_{<\theta}$. Which features of the ordinal tail of
$\theta$, beyond $|\theta|$ and $|\No_{<\theta}|$, survive in its coding
rank and local character?
\end{question}
The cone argument for an initial cardinal relies on closure under
$i+1+\alpha$ below the cutoff. At a noncardinal cutoff that closure can
fail and should be replaced by a stratified family of cones.

\begin{question}[Isomorphism, not merely equimorphism]\label{swo:st:n14.3}
Classify the order topology and isomorphism invariants of
$\WO_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$. At regular cutoffs, and at singular strong limits,
what are its density, cellularity, cut-character spectra, and degrees of
homogeneity? Which distinguish it from other orders of the same binary
rank?
\end{question}
The binary cube itself cannot be the literal answer: it has endpoints
and adjacent pairs, while the surreal permutation order has different
local behavior. A dense suborder equimorphic with a cube can retain
substantial information not measured by rank.

\begin{question}[The hierarchy of proper-class blocks]\label{swo:st:n14.4}
Study the subpredicates of $\Hall(\No)$ with types
$\Ord\cdot\gamma+\alpha$ for fixed set ordinals $\gamma,\alpha$.
Give explicit, size-safe embedding and nonembedding theorems between
these subpredicates and the set-like order.
\end{question}
The inaccessible-model calculation provides concrete bounded targets and
shows that the full order is strictly more complex than the set-like
order there. Extending binary fusion to uniform transformations on
class predicates may require stronger comprehension; that dependence
should be proved, not assumed away.

\begin{remark}[Source 12's question ``The exact weak-choice strength'', answered]\label{swo:st:n14.5}
\emph{Source 12's text:} Remove set-level AC from the base theory in \cref{swo:st:thm:choice}. What
principle is equivalent to a class well-order of the sign-sequence
surreals then? Compare it with coherent well-ordering of power sets of
ordinals and with uniform ordinal presentations of transitive closures.

\merge\ \emph{Answered (2 October 2026).} Source 11's \cref{swo:cf:choice} proves the
equivalence over GB with no set-level choice: a class well-order of the
sign-sequence surreals is equivalent to global choice. Its proof is
precisely a uniform well-ordering of the power sets $V_{\beta+1}$,
obtained by set-valued recursion from the given well-order on the sign
sequences of each length $\theta$; see \cref{swo:rem:answered-choice}.
(Corrected on 3 October 2026 after the Hilbert's-tenth review
\path{review_surreal_synthesis_0be9b9134.md}: ``uniform'' replaces
``coherent'', since these orders need not extend one another;
\cref{swo:rem:answered-choice} gives a finite example.)
\end{remark}
This is separate from the question whether surreal universality for
class linear orders itself implies global choice, raised by Hamkins
\cite{HamkinsUnivChoice}. The present equivalence concerns a well-order of
all surreal labels and does not settle that universality question.

\begin{question}[Elementary common-prefix theory]\label{swo:st:n14.6}
Formalize \cref{swo:st:thm:fulllex} over a precisely chosen weak class theory.
How little comprehension and class well-foundedness are needed? Can one
characterize the same relation directly by a formula avoiding explicit
mention of the common-prefix class?
\end{question}
The definition already expands to elementary quantifiers. A mechanized
proof would make the separation from abstract class comparability
particularly transparent and yield a reusable theorem for other carriers.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms and finite condensation]\label{swo:st:n14.7}
Determine natural automorphism groups of the full lexicographic order,
and of the order after collapsing finite residual blocks. Which
operations arise from numerical automorphisms or permutations of the
underlying surreal carrier, and which genuinely act on enumeration
structure?
\end{question}
Finite-tail blocks are now characterized intrinsically by adjacency.
That makes condensation a plausible first invariant, but no complete
classification of its quotient is claimed here.

\begin{question}[Dependence on the class realization]\label{swo:st:n14.8}
Fix a transitive set universe $M$ and vary its admissible class collection
$\mathcal X$. Which external order invariants of the admitted global
well-orders detect this change? Can the order reconstruct useful
information about available truth predicates or class choice functions?
\end{question}
The diagonal obstruction persists internally, while external cardinality
can vary. This makes the distinction between full and Henkin semantics a
source of mathematical questions rather than merely a formal warning.

\begin{question}[Compatibility between birthday cutoffs]\label{swo:st:n14.9}
Construct and analyze coherent embeddings from the well-order spaces at
smaller birthday cutoffs into those at larger cutoffs. Which choices of
reserve labels and tail enumerations are functorial, and which preserve
finite condensation, coding ranks, or canonical cylinders?
\end{question}
Naively extending every enumeration by an arbitrary tail can change
minimal length, and fixed choices need not be compatible across three
cutoffs. A coherence theorem would make universe-lifting arguments much
more useful in a proof assistant.

\subsection{Source 09's research directions}
\label{swo:ec:sec:research}
The following are proposed problems emerging from the development, not
a claim that all are already catalogued open problems. Each is stated
with a foundational level so that its intended meaning is clear.

\subsubsection{Formal proof of the surreal core theorem}
\textbf{Framework:} universe-indexed Lean with explicit smallness and a
baseline parameter. Complete the prefix-extension and interpolation
modules, then prove the back-and-forth isomorphism. The difficult part
is expected to be the bookkeeping of small histories and variable
ordinal prefixes, not the finite first-disagreement arguments. A useful
first milestone is the inaccessible or regular-cardinal set-sized
version, parameterized by an abstract saturated alphabet.

\subsubsection{Exact axiomatic strength of the global conclusions}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GB$ with ordinary set choice but without global
choice. \Cref{swo:ec:prop:baseline-choice} settles the baseline question: a
set-like global well-order of $\No$ is equivalent to global choice.
Determine the exact strength of alternative universality and homogeneity
assertions that do not already assume such a baseline. In particular,
which conclusions can be stated and proved for individually definable
class orders without supplying a single uniform global enumeration?
Distinguish uniform existence assertions from a schema treating one
fixed definition at a time; the latter is not automatically a uniform
class construction.

\subsubsection{Which cuts of the core represent exhaustive branches?}
\textbf{Framework:} class cut parameters over $\Psupp(b)$ or an explicitly
higher-sorted completion. Every global enumeration determines a cut
in the dense core, and density makes this representation injective.
Characterize its image intrinsically. The missing-branch construction
shows that injectivity of a class word is insufficient: exhaustiveness
must be detected. A promising formulation separates coherence of set
prefixes, realizability of each next-coordinate cut, and eventual
coverage of every surreal value.

\subsubsection{Automorphisms beyond set-sized partial maps}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GBC$ for the core; higher-sort or universe-bounded
versions for the full comparison object. Set-sized partial
isomorphisms extend in the core, but proper-class partial maps need not.
Classify which preserve enough prefix or support structure to extend.
Also distinguish automorphisms of the bare order from those preserving
the preferred filtration by support bounds. These are different
classification problems even though the bare core is always $\No$.

\subsubsection{Non-set-like well-order relations}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GBC$ or $\GBC+\ETR$, with a fixed relation-code
coordinate order. Study the alternative binary comparison of all global
well-order relations. Which order properties depend on the coordinate
enumeration? Does it contain a natural set-coded dense core, and when
are its cuts represented by actual class well-orders? No conclusion
about that different comparison follows merely from the enumeration
results proved here.

\subsubsection{Sharp birthday and support bounds}
\textbf{Framework:} $\ZFC$ on bounded fragments. Given bounds on the
birthdays and first-disagreement coordinates of a set family, determine
optimal bounds for an interpolating prefix and its supported completion.
The present proof bounds the forced prefix length by
$\sup\{\Delta(E_i,F_j)+1:i\in I,j\in J\}+1$ and uses an oversized
cardinal for support. That bound is
safe but not generally minimal. This direction could yield concrete
complexity estimates for symbolic surreal order calculations.

\subsubsection{What survives away from inaccessible truncations?}
\textbf{Framework:} $\ZFC$ with specified cardinal arithmetic. Replace
the inaccessible $\kappa$ by a regular cardinal and a set alphabet with
appropriate cut saturation. Separate the roles of regularity,
$\kappa^{<\kappa}=\kappa$, and closure under the required cut constructor.
At singular cardinals, the first-disagreement bound can reach the
ambient length even for relatively small families; identify the
resulting interpolation spectrum and construct sharp counterexamples.

\subsubsection{Other termination conventions for set words}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GBC$ or bounded $\ZFC$. Our dictionary order makes
proper prefixes smaller and therefore creates the limit-prefix
suprema of \cref{swo:ec:prop:prefix-cf}. Study a distinguished internal
termination value, restricted alphabets, or prefix-free codes of set
well-orders. Determine exactly which variants have the set-cut property
and hence are isomorphic to $\No$. The convention must be part of the
statement, not an implicit analogy with surreal signs.

\subsubsection{Uniform infinitary constructions indexed by redundant codes}
\textbf{Framework:} bounded universes first. Kanovei--Shelah-style
redundant indexing suggests avoiding a choice of one representative
for each well-order or auxiliary object. Investigate constructions
using the support core or bounded strata as indices, while checking
that the resulting products, functions, and quotient relations remain
at the declared level. The diagonal theorem forbids a uniform
same-level list of all global enumerations, but does not preclude
purpose-built redundant families adequate for a particular theorem.

\subsection{Source 08's research questions and topics}\label{swo:sk:sec:research}

The following are directions not resolved by the present manuscript.
They are not blanket assertions that no relevant answer exists in the
literature. Each should begin with a targeted literature search and a
precise choice of size level.

\subsubsection{Set-sized enumeration orders}

\paragraph{1. Isomorphism classification beyond the common spectrum.}
The ordinal spectrum and cardinality of $\W(X)$ depend only on $|X|$,
while its local cylinder structure remembers the numerical order of
residual alphabets. Which additional invariants of $X$ can be recovered
from $\W(X)$? Determine sufficient and necessary conditions for
$\W(X)\cong\W(Y)$, rather than merely embeddings in both directions.
Dense alphabets, well-orders, and mixed sums provide natural test cases.

\paragraph{2. Exact invariants at regular cutoffs (\merge\ partly answered; answered 3 October 2026; see the notes after this list).}
For regular $\kappa$ with $2^{<\kappa}=\kappa$, compute the density,
cellularity, point characters, and cut cofinalities of
$\W_\kappa(\No_{<\kappa})$. The binary equimorphism in \eqref{swo:sk:eq:t6} does not by
itself determine its order-topological isomorphism type. Investigate
whether the support skeleton construction has a natural $\kappa$-sized
dense realization inside this set order under weaker assumptions than
strong inaccessibility.

\paragraph{3. Singular birthdays and code lengths (\merge\ answered in part; see the notes after this list).}
At singular $\kappa$, exactly which cuts of size below $\kappa$ fail to
be realized in $\No_{<\kappa}$ or in its fixed-length enumeration
order? Determine the least binary coding lengths for these orders and
how they depend on cofinality and cardinal arithmetic. The three
specific uses of regularity in \cref{swo:sk:thm:cutoff} identify where a new
argument is needed.

\paragraph{4. Prescribed noninitial lengths.}
For $\alpha$ of cardinality $\kappa$, classify
$\W_\alpha(\No_{<\lambda})$. Finite tails are understood through
\cref{swo:sk:thm:adjacent}, but noninitial limit lengths may preserve finer
lexicographic complexity. Compare this problem with the fixed-type
analysis proposed in the continuum manuscript \cite{Batch76Source02}, checking
its hypotheses and proofs independently for nonseparable alphabets.

\subsubsection{The skeleton and the virtual ambient order}

\paragraph{5. Definable choices of the surreal isomorphism.}
The back-and-forth isomorphism $\Psupp(b)\cong\No$ depends on witness
choices. With a specified global well-order, can it be chosen to
respect useful support or birthday bounds? What additional
normalization gives uniqueness, if any? Distinguish definability from
parameters, parameter-free definability, and invariance under a change
of baseline.

\paragraph{6. Automorphisms and extension from a skeleton.}
An order automorphism $\varphi$ of $\No$ acts on $\Hsl$ by
$e\mapsto\varphi\circ e$ and sends $O_b$ onto $O_{\varphi\circ b}$.
Which automorphisms of one skeleton extend to uniform automorphisms of
the full virtual order? Can order alone recognize eventual-agreement
orbits, or are these additional structure supplied by the coordinate
presentation?

\paragraph{7. Full virtual lexicographic products (\merge\ answered 3 October 2026; see the notes after this list).}
For an ordinary class carrier, every set-indexed lexicographic power
of $\No$ embeds into a skeleton. The \emph{full virtual} product
$\Hsl\times_{\lex}\Hsl$ is a different object. Does it admit a uniform
order embedding into $\Hsl$? More generally, determine an absorption
spectrum for uniform virtual powers. Simply concatenating two
$\Ord$-long words has domain $\Ord+\Ord$, not a set-like $\Ord$
domain, so the set-sized concatenation argument is unavailable.

\paragraph{8. Higher-size cuts and completion (\merge\ answered 3 October 2026 for cuts of the core; see the notes after this list).}
The set-cut theorem deliberately leaves out cuts specified by proper
class families of enumeration codes or by higher collections of
classes. Classify which such cuts are realized once a precise
higher-type language is chosen. A proposed Dedekind completion must
identify the type of its cut objects and cannot be treated as another
ordinary class without a size proof.

\paragraph{9. Classification of relation-code orders.}
For two global coordinate enumerations $q,q'$ of $\No^2$, the
relation-code orders have the same binary equimorphism type. Are there
useful hypotheses yielding an isomorphism? Determine which invariants
are artifacts of the coordinate order and which reflect genuine
properties of class well-orders.

\subsubsection{Foundations and formalization}

\paragraph{10. Minimal axioms, stated theorem by theorem.}
Separate the strength of a baseline $\Ord\cong\No$, uniform prefix
completion, orbit cut filling, and the global back-and-forth theorem.
Over variants of $\GB$ with set Choice, which global selection
principles are necessary for their uniform formulations? The present
proofs establish sufficiency of $\GBC$, not an exact reverse-mathematical
classification.

\paragraph{11. Comparison of non-set-like class well-orders (\merge\ answered; see the note after this list).}
Formulate an explicit alignment or comparison principle for arbitrary
class well-orders and locate its recursion requirements. Which
restricted domains, such as finite sums of $\Ord$ and set ordinals,
admit direct elementary algorithms? A theorem about all class domains
should not be extrapolated from these examples without proof.

\paragraph{12. Dependence on the class collection.}
For fixed $M$ and $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D$, compare the virtual
orders of global enumerations in $(M,\mathcal C)$ and
$(M,\mathcal D)$. The same set-coded skeleton relative to a shared
baseline remains available, but new class rows may appear. Study which
higher-size cut properties, operator embeddings, and definability
properties change.

\paragraph{13. Quantitative and certified prefix extension.}
Formalize the support bound in \cref{swo:sk:lem:extension}, the forced-prefix
length in \cref{swo:sk:thm:orbitcut}, and the birthday of its stopping entry.
This would make the central theorem a sequence of explicit bounded
lemmas rather than one monolithic existence proof. It is a strong
first target for the repository's existing small-cut interface.

\paragraph{14. Increasing-subset and alternate-termination orders (\merge\ answered 3 October 2026 except one type; see the notes after this list).}
Study lexicographic orders of numerically increasing set sequences,
as opposed to arbitrary enumerations, and compare prefix-small,
prefix-large, and centered-termination conventions. The limit-prefix
counterexample shows that these choices affect local cofinalities even
when the alphabet is $\No$.

\paragraph{15. An order-theoretic interface for class nonstandard models.}
Determine which part of a Kanovei--Shelah-style indexing construction
can use a set-coded skeleton and which genuinely needs a larger
collection. Keep the order embedding problem separate from the
existence of a class ultrafilter, satisfaction relation, or transfer
principle. A successful construction should include an explicit
uniform-family and smallness audit at every step.

\subsection{Source 13: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:fs:sec:questions}

These questions are proposed continuations of the present development,
not a claim that each is a previously published open problem. The
prefix-trace criterion, the first-failure classification, and the
negative pure-order cylinder result settle the versions stated here;
the questions below ask for stronger or different conclusions.

\subsubsection{Cuts, trees, and enriched structure}

\begin{question}[Minimal extra structure for recognizing branches]\label{swo:fs:n15.1}
What is the weakest expansion of the pure core order $\Psupp(b)\cong\No$
that makes its branch traces recognizable? Is the family of all
cylinders enough as an unranked family, or must one retain the
prefix-length relation? Can a support filtration recover the necessary
levels without explicitly naming prefixes?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:fs:thm:nonrigidity} shows that the pure order alone cannot
canonically recover the original cylinder family. The positive target
is therefore an enriched reconstruction theorem, not a repetition of
the disproved pure-order assertion.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms preserving a chosen core]\label{swo:fs:n15.2}
Classify the uniform order automorphisms of $\Hsl$ that preserve the
specific eventual-agreement core $\Psupp(b)$. Which preserve its support
filtration, and which preserve the set of exhaustive traces after an
isomorphism between two cores? Does adding birthday or simplicity
information force a substantial rigidity theorem?
\end{question}
The finite-block automorphisms need not preserve the baseline orbit.
A useful initial project is to characterize tail alphabet
transformations that do preserve it.

\begin{question}[A normal form for class cuts]\label{swo:fs:n15.3}
Can the branch/horizontal/limit-boundary trichotomy be organized into a
canonical recursive notation for every available normalized cut?
For horizontal cuts, how much of the next-label cut can be encoded by
surreal simplicity data? What uniqueness survives when changes of
prefix presentation are allowed?
\end{question}
A complete class-cut collection is not an ordinary class object in
$\GBC$. The first implementation should concern one supplied class cut
or one uniform class-indexed family, before introducing a higher sort.

\begin{question}[Sharp cutoff analogues]\label{swo:fs:n15.4}
For a birthday fragment $X_\kappa$, determine which part of the
first-failure classification survives when prefix extension can fail
through exhaustion, complement-cardinality mismatch, or a missing
label separator. Can these three obstructions be combined with the
singular strong-limit transition into a practical classification of
cut characters in fixed-length strata?
\end{question}
This asks for more than substituting $X_\kappa$ into the global theorem;
the hypotheses that must be replaced are explicitly identified in
\Cref{swo:fs:swf:sec:fixed}.

\subsubsection{Products, comprehension, and model dependence}

\begin{question}[The weakest uniform split obstruction]\label{swo:fs:n15.5}
Over $\GBC$, what additional comprehension principle suffices to rule
out a fixed-formula uniform embedding $\Hsl\times_{\lex}2\to \Hsl$?
Can the inverse-evaluator argument be reduced to a restricted
existential-class comprehension schema? For more restrictive formulas
defining the proposed embedding, is there an elementary diagonal
argument avoiding that comprehension altogether?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:fs:thm:kmsplit} gives a sufficient theory and identifies
the point to optimize. It is not a proof that full $\KM$ is necessary.

\begin{question}[A hierarchy beyond one split]\label{swo:fs:n15.6}
In a full inaccessible universe, classify the mutual embeddability
of ${\Hsl}^n_{\lex}$ for finite $n\geq2$, of $\Hsl\times_{\lex}K$ for
various right factors $K$, and of iterated point-splittings. Which
invariants distinguish these orders after the first dense-core
obstruction has saturated at cardinality $2^\kappa$?
\end{question}
All these orders can have the same cardinality, so a useful invariant
must record more than the number of elements. Families of disjoint
intervals, patterns of adjacent pairs, and iterated condensation are
natural candidates.

\begin{question}[Class realizations with intermediate behavior]\label{swo:fs:n15.7}
For a fixed set model $M$, how do different collections of available
classes $\mathcal C$ affect the external density, cellularity, and
product-embedding behavior of its enumeration order? Which
intermediate behaviors lie between the externally countable rational
case and the full inaccessible-universe obstruction?
\end{question}
A precise answer should state whether a map is arbitrary external,
definable over the two-sorted model, or coded in an additional sort.
Those are distinct classification problems.

\begin{question}[Uniformity versus external isomorphism]\label{swo:fs:n15.8}
For an externally countable model, can the complexity of an external
isomorphism $\Hsl\cong\mathbb Q$ be measured relative to presentations
of its set and class sorts? What information about the model is
necessary to compute, define, or select such an isomorphism?
\end{question}
This connects the order-theoretic collapse to computability and model
presentation without mistaking an external construction for a class
available internally.

\subsubsection{Termination, bounds, and residual orders}

\begin{question}[A classification of termination cuts]\label{swo:fs:n15.9}
For a class alphabet order-isomorphic to $\No$, characterize the
placements of an extra terminal marker for which arbitrary set-word
or injective set-word lexicography is set-cut saturated. What happens
when the marker is placed immediately on one side of an existing
label, rather than reserving that label? Can the answer be expressed
in terms of the two characters of the marker cut?
\end{question}
The end-first and end-last failures and the reserved-central success
are settled here. They need not exhaust all intermediate behavior.

\begin{question}[Optimal birthday and support bounds]\label{swo:fs:n15.10}
For prescribed bounds on input birthdays, word length, and baseline
indices, sharpen the prefix-length and support-cardinality bounds in
\Cref{swo:fs:thm:interpolate}. Is the explicit central-code birthday
sum optimal within a useful class of prefix-free local codes? Which
bounds are compatible with embeddings across birthday cutoffs?
\end{question}
The current support completion deliberately chooses a large cardinal
to equalize complements. It proves existence, not optimality.

\begin{question}[Iterating raw residual decomposition]\label{swo:fs:n15.11}
The ordinal-head fiber theorem removes one set-like initial part.
How far can residual decomposition be iterated with set-valued codes,
and what class-recursion principles are needed when an iteration has
class-valued stages? Is there a canonical rank or notation for a
substantial family of raw class well-orders beyond the first head?
\end{question}
This is where $\ETR$ or a stronger scheme could become genuinely
relevant. The elementary one-head construction alone does not justify
an arbitrary iteration.

\begin{question}[Relation-code dependence]\label{swo:fs:n15.12}
For two set-like enumerations of pairs, determine which
transformations relate their relation-bit orders on raw well-orders.
When do the two induced orders become isomorphic, merely equimorphic,
or distinct under definability restrictions? Which code orders can
be characterized by simple invariants of the pair enumeration?
\end{question}

\subsubsection{A concrete formalization milestone}

\begin{question}[First checked extension]\label{swo:fs:n15.13}
Formalize the split-order density lemma and the crossing-prefix
uniqueness/reconstruction argument in a size-explicit abstract setting.
Then instantiate the small-cut and fresh-value interfaces using
\code{SignSequenceCut.lean}. Can the central-word saturation theorem
be completed without introducing surreal field arithmetic?
\end{question}
The answer to the last design question should be positive at the
mathematical level: the proof uses only order, the reserved marker,
smallness, and fresh set-cut separators. Establishing this dependency
boundary in Lean would be a useful substantial first checked result.

\subsection{Source 14: further research questions and priorities}
\label{swo:tc:sec:questions}
The following are proposed continuations of the present work. They are
not all established named open problems in the literature. In particular,
the prefix-structured exhaustive-cut question and the support-cardinal
threshold are now answered by the theorems above; the questions here
state stronger or different targets rather than restating those results.

\subsubsection{Cut recognition beyond the named prefix structure}
\begin{question}[The exhaustive-trace stabilizer]\label{swo:tc:n14.1}
Characterize the subgroup of class order automorphisms of $\Psupp(b)$
that preserves the exhaustive-trace collection. How does it compare
with the groups preserving all prefix cylinders, or all label incidences?
Can it be generated by explicit transformations of enumeration structure?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:tc:thm:orbits} classifies the bare-order cut orbits and
\Cref{swo:tc:cor:nonintrinsic} proves that this stabilizer is proper.
What remains is its structure, not the now-answered yes/no question
whether every core automorphism preserves exhaustive representability.

\begin{question}[Minimal enrichment for exhaustiveness]\label{swo:tc:n14.2}
Can the coverage predicate be recovered from cylinder inclusion and
numerical order of children without naming the label evaluation itself?
What additional incidence relation records that the same surreal label
appears at different possible coordinates?
\end{question}
Coherence is essentially a branch property of the cylinder tree, whereas
exhaustiveness compares labels along that branch with the entire
alphabet. Separating these logical resources should clarify exactly
what the recognition theorem uses.

\subsubsection{The support hierarchy beyond one saturation invariant}
\begin{question}[Isomorphism of support layers]\label{swo:tc:n14.3}
For infinite cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$ with
$\cf\kappa=\cf\lambda$, when are
$\mathcal P_{<\kappa}(b)$ and $\mathcal P_{<\lambda}(b)$ isomorphic
as bare class linear orders? Does some cut invariant recover more than
the cofinality of the support threshold?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:tc:thm:support} separates layers with different cofinalities
but leaves this equal-cofinality case untouched. Their shared embedded
copy of $\No$ is too weak to decide it. The attained minimum support
cost is an invariant of the \emph{support-enriched} structure, not yet
an invariant of its bare order.

\begin{question}[Support ideals]\label{swo:tc:n14.4}
Replace the cardinality condition by an ideal of permitted set supports.
Under what closure and permutation-invariance hypotheses is saturation
controlled by the ideal's additivity? Can a failure of union closure
always be converted into a coherent prefix configuration forcing a
support outside the ideal?
\end{question}
The compression lemma bounds cardinality, not membership in an arbitrary
ideal: it can adjoin images of moved coordinates and a buffer. Therefore
a general ideal theorem needs explicit closure under those operations.
It would be incorrect simply to replace $<\kappa$ by ``belongs to the
ideal'' in the existing proof.

\begin{question}[Optimal simultaneous support cost]\label{swo:tc:n14.5}
Given a specific separated set family, characterize the least support
cardinality of a separator by its forced-prefix tree, rather than only
by the union of all input supports. Can the finite version be computed
without enumerating all possible separator permutations?
\end{question}
The sharp examples attain the threshold, but many input supports contain
coordinates irrelevant to their comparisons. The first-outside-support
argument suggests an algorithmic pruning principle. Finite optimization
and the transfinite cardinal minimum should be studied separately.

\subsubsection{Raw tails, condensation, and alternative comparison orders}
\begin{question}[Iterated initial-branch quotients]\label{swo:tc:n14.6}
After quotienting raw well-orders by their first $\Ord$-long branch,
can one iterate a similarly explicit trace construction to recover
successive proper-class blocks? What can be proved for prescribed
block patterns without assuming a canonical class ordinal for every
well-order?
\end{question}
The trace-fiber theorem completely describes the first loss of
information. Iterating it along class-valued histories may require
stronger recursion principles. The exact point at which elementary
comprehension ceases to suffice should be isolated as a theorem.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms of raw trace fibers]\label{swo:tc:n14.7}
Which automorphisms of the branch order extend to the unrestricted
well-order order, and what compatibility conditions do the residual
alphabets impose? Which automorphisms preserve finite residual blocks
but fail to preserve the core-trace quotient?
\end{question}
The singleton omitted-label fiber shows that being a singleton is not
enough to recognize the exhaustive suborder. Any extension theorem must
also account for residual alphabets with more than one label.

\begin{question}[Relation-code comparison]\label{swo:tc:n14.8}
For a specified coordinate schedule on pairs of surreal labels, classify
the class cuts represented by genuine well-order relations. Is there a
useful analogue of crossing cylinders that detects transitivity,
linearity, and well-foundedness from a coherent branch of relation bits?
\end{question}
Coherent binary bits always define a relation, but well-foundedness is a
global constraint. The strong reconstruction phenomenon for exhaustive
enumerations may not carry over. A schedule-independent theorem must
explicitly quantify which coordinate changes it tolerates.

\subsubsection{Birthday cutoffs and universe coherence}
\begin{question}[Exact local geometry of set slices]\label{swo:tc:n14.9}
For $\mu=2^{<\kappa}$, determine the complete cut-character spectrum of
$\W_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$, especially when $\mu>\kappa$ and at
singular cutoffs. Which parts of the crossing-cylinder proof survive
when deleting a long used prefix can exhaust intervals of the alphabet?
\end{question}
This continues an unfilled target of the predecessor. The global proof
uses the fact that deleting \emph{any set} leaves plentiful fresh
surreals; a fixed birthday fragment lacks that unrestricted property.
The inherited binary equimorphism does not decide the local characters.

\begin{question}[Coherent embeddings across cutoffs]\label{swo:tc:n14.10}
Construct explicit embeddings between enumeration spaces for increasing
birthday bounds that compose coherently. Which preserve the minimal
allowed enumeration type, the prefix cylinders, or the relevant support
filtration?
\end{question}
Appending an arbitrary tail preserves a first disagreement but may
change the ordinal type. A functorial construction should record both
the alphabet inclusion and the position schedule, rather than silently
identify cardinally equivalent domains.

\subsubsection{Class realizations and proof strength}
\begin{question}[Which new cuts can a class extension add?]\label{swo:tc:n14.11}
For a fixed set model and old baseline, characterize the additional
exhaustive trace cuts admitted by specified class extensions. Can the
new-cut collection distinguish natural classes of realizations even
when their old-cut realizability relations agree?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:tc:thm:absolute} supplies a rigidity constraint: no old cut
changes status. It does not classify the new parameters. The tail fibers
also suggest studying extensions that add raw orders with an old trace
but a new tail.

\begin{question}[Axiomatic economy]\label{swo:tc:n14.12}
What is the weakest class theory proving the crossing-chain trichotomy
and its reconstruction theorem once a baseline and fresh-separator
property are supplied? Can the proof of the support threshold be
formalized in a set-only regular-cardinal model before passing to
classes?
\end{question}
The existing proofs visibly use elementary comprehension and class
Replacement, plus set Choice for extensions. Identifying which are
essential is more informative than merely observing that a stronger
class theory also proves the theorem.

\begin{question}[First kernel-verified milestone]\label{swo:tc:n14.13}
Can the common-prefix comparison and the support-compression lemma be
formalized as small reusable Lean modules, then independently connected
to the pinned surreal sign-sequence library?
\end{question}
These targets avoid the largest foundational infrastructure while
capturing the most error-prone finite and cardinal bookkeeping. A
useful deliverable would include separate tests for fixed-position
preservation, complement cardinalities, and the distinction between
strict right character and the character of a normalized cut complement.

\subsection{Source 15: further research questions and a prioritized program}\label{swo:cb:sec:questions}

\begin{question}[All fixed enumeration types]\label{swo:cb:n13.1}
Write $\alpha=\mu\cdot\gamma+\zeta$ with $\zeta<\mu$ infinite.
Classify the possible residual numerical suborders left after the long
prefix, and use them to compute $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})$.
The theorem here handles exactly finite $\zeta$. A useful first family
is $\zeta=\omega$, followed by regular and singular infinite remainders.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday bounds]\label{swo:cb:n13.2}
For an arbitrary ordinal $\theta$, determine the order structure of
$\No_{<\theta}$ and its permutation strata. The cone and ordinal
absorption arguments for an initial cardinal need not survive unchanged.
Identify which ordinal invariants of $\theta$ replace the present
regular/singular dichotomy.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[The exact strength of arbitrary-input condensation]\label{swo:cb:n13.3}
Does GB prove a uniform class coding all finite condensations of every
class well-order? If not, determine a sharp sufficient and necessary
principle. Then study longer histories with specified limit intersections.
The explicit polynomial examples show that existence for particular long
histories alone is insufficient to calibrate the general scheme.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Intrinsic information in the full raw order]\label{swo:cb:n13.4}
Which prefix cones, first-block fibres, and finite residual blocks are
definable from the bare lexicographic order of raw well-orders?
\Cref{swo:cb:thm:automorphism} shows that the abstract core does not
determine its represented cuts. Determine how much extra structure is
needed for reconstruction, and whether the full raw order restores any
of the lost distinctions.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Completion with residual data]\label{swo:cb:n13.5}
Construct and characterize a stratified completion that contains all
terminal cuts while recording the residual well-order fibres over persistent
branches. Determine its universal property and its minimum required size
level. Ordinary Dedekind completion alone loses the residual data.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Automorphism extension]\label{swo:cb:n13.6}
Characterize those automorphisms of a bounded-support core that preserve
persistent cuts, preserve exhaustive cuts, or extend to native global
enumerations. Compare cores built from baselines differing on a proper
class of positions. The abstract isomorphism of two cores does not decide
their placement inside the surrounding order.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Finer topology of bounded slices]\label{swo:cb:n13.7}
After the density, cellularity, and point-character calculations, classify
the exact gap spectra, local bases, and isomorphism types of the bounded
permutation spaces. Equimorphism with a binary product does not determine
all these invariants. Study which distinctions survive when cardinal
arithmetic makes displayed density values coincide.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Inverse ranks and prescribed relation scans]\label{swo:cb:n13.8}
Classify the cuts and point characters of ordinal-rank lexicography beyond
the points $M_\lambda$. For table lexicography, use endpoint transfer to
characterize scans whose extremal linear-order table is well-founded or
set-like. Then seek invariants beyond the three possible endpoint patterns.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Coherent restricted filtrations]\label{swo:cb:n13.9}
The three-label theorem rules out monotonicity for every restriction.
Which nested chains of carriers, or which restricted families of orders,
admit a useful monotone restriction system? Can birthday cutoffs be linked
by canonical order embeddings rather than by unrestricted deletion?
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Naturally well-ordered supports]\label{swo:cb:n13.10}
Characterize the image and omitted cuts of
$A\mapsto-\sum_{a\in A}\omega^{-a}$. Compare shorter-first and
longer-first orders on increasing set words, and develop a higher-level
analogue that treats proper-class supports without calling the result a
single surreal normal form.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Class-model dependence]\label{swo:cb:n13.11}
For a fixed set universe $M$, study changes in the lexicographic theory as
the class realization grows from $\mathcal C$ to $\mathcal C'$.
Which statements about existing orders are absolute, which require
well-foundedness preservation, and which detect newly available cuts or
enumerations? Keep full-class and Henkin interpretations separate.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[First formal milestones]\label{swo:cb:n13.12}
Formalize the set-prefix common-disagreement formula and the elementary
set-interval quotient before the entire class theory. Next verify the
binary scheduler and finite-fibre fusion; then the persistent-cut
reconstruction with explicit smallness. These have concise interfaces and
clear failure cases, making them useful independent additions to ProveIt.
\end{question}

The most concrete next mathematical projects are the smaller infinite-tail
classification, exact bounded gap spectra, and the automorphism-extension
criterion. The most concrete foundational project is the arbitrary-input
condensation scheme. Each now has a precise point where the proved
construction stops, rather than an undifferentiated request to study
``all well-orders.''

\Cref{swo:cb:n13.1,swo:cb:n13.2} are source~12's
\cref{swo:st:n14.1,swo:st:n14.2} beyond the cases answered in Part~VI. The
others remain open.

\subsection{Source 16: further research questions, with the resolved parts removed}
\label{swo:ds:sec:research}

The following are proposed continuation problems, not a census of
currently open problems in the literature. In particular, the exact
termination family, represented-cut recognition with the labelled prefix
tree, simultaneous residual blocks, and the stated regular-stage
topological invariants have been settled under the assumptions of this
article. They should not be relisted as wholly open.

\subsubsection{Highest-priority structural problems}

\begin{question}[Longer-stratum binary coding ranks]\label{swo:ds:n16.1}
For $\No_{<\kappa}$ and $\mu=2^{<\kappa}$, determine the least
ordinal $\rho$ for which $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})\emb2^\rho_{\lex}$ for
every $|\alpha|=\mu$, and determine the reverse cube embeddings.
\end{question}
The topology is now known for all these strata, but it does not determine
binary coding rank. The singular strong-limit transition
\eqref{swo:ds:eq:singular} and the finite residual permutation blocks give
concrete starting cases. The first targets should be $\alpha=\mu+1$,
$\mu+2$, and $\mu+\omega$, with separate treatment of singular
strong-limit $\kappa$.

\begin{question}[Singular birthday gaps]\label{swo:ds:n16.2}
Determine the unfilled cut-character spectrum of
$\WO_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$ when $\kappa$ is singular, and when $\kappa$ is
regular but $\mu>\kappa$.
\end{question}
The global characters $\cf(\kappa)$ and the exact density
$\mu^{<\mu}$ are known here. The missing information is local: which
numerical gaps in the truncated alphabet combine with exhaustion and
prefix edges to produce each pair of cofinalities? The bounded
first-failure analysis should be formulated before attempting a general
classification by cardinal arithmetic alone.

\begin{question}[Centered increasing words]\label{swo:ds:n16.3}
Classify the order of numerically increasing set-length words when the
termination symbol is placed at a fixed interior numerical threshold.
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:ds:thm:alltermination} covers unrestricted and injective
words. The increasing case has prefix-dependent available alphabets and
already fails the centered saturation theorem. A useful first problem is
to determine all point characters for the $0^-$ and $0^+$ placements,
including words that cross the threshold only at a limit stage.

\begin{question}[Recovering prefix structure from order alone]\label{swo:ds:n16.4}
Which features of the labelled prefix tree can be reconstructed from the
bare order $\Pbd(b)$, from $\Hsl$ as a definable comparison, or from $\Hall$?
\end{question}
Our cut recognition uses the family of cylinders and numerical labels as
extra predicates. A bare core is isomorphic to $\No$, and singleton
raw fibers can arise either from an exhaustive branch or from a branch
omitting one label. Thus neither the core order nor the size of a fiber
immediately identifies exhaustion. One can ask for the least additional
predicates that make the tree and exhaustion relation definable.

\begin{question}[Changing baselines and extending automorphisms]\label{swo:ds:n16.5}
For two baselines $b,c$, characterize when an automorphism of the
set-like global comparison carries $\Pbd(b)$ onto
$\Pbd(c)$.
\end{question}
An increasing numerical automorphism $h$ gives the explicit example
$E\mapsto h\circ E$, carrying $\Pbd(b)$ onto
$\Pbd(h\circ b)$. General abstract isomorphisms between the
two cores need not preserve the distinguished set of exhaustive
branch cuts. \Cref{swo:ds:thm:cutrecognition} suggests an extension
criterion stated in terms of precisely those cuts.

\subsubsection{Foundational problems with explicit targets}

\begin{question}[Exact strength of uniform nonembedding]\label{swo:ds:n16.6}
Can the conclusion of \Cref{swo:ds:thm:sigma} for elementary
transformation formulas be proved in GBC alone? If not, what is its
reverse-mathematical strength?
\end{question}
The missing step is sharply localized: forming the inverse evaluator
\eqref{swo:ds:eq:inverseeval}. A lower bound would need a model in which a
specified elementary transformation exists or a reduction from a
comprehension principle. The mere presence of an existential class
quantifier in the present proof does not establish necessity.

\begin{question}[Repeated condensation of the quotient]\label{swo:ds:n16.7}
Determine the strength and possible stabilization behavior of the
transfinite tower obtained by repeatedly taking least representatives
of set-interval blocks and intersecting at limits.
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:ds:thm:blocks} has removed the need for ETR to extract all
blocks of one order. The new question concerns repeated condensation
of the resulting index orders. Suitable ETR is a sufficient bound;
whether this particular operator needs it, and which class orders can
remain nontrivial at prescribed stages, are separate questions.

\begin{question}[Choice needed for the word isomorphisms]\label{swo:ds:n16.8}
How far can \Cref{swo:ds:thm:wordisomorphism,swo:ds:thm:alltermination} be proved without a global well-order?
\end{question}
Their explicit embeddings and the termination saturation criterion use
less than the GBC back-and-forth isomorphisms. Investigate whether
set choice, a restricted class-enumeration principle, or a canonical
sign construction suffices for particular cases. This does not settle
the broader historical question about the choice strength of universal
embeddability into $\No$.

\begin{question}[Class extensions and canonical data]\label{swo:ds:n16.9}
For a fixed set universe with two admitted-class expansions, describe
which new branch cuts, global well-orders, and uniform transformations
become available.
\end{question}
Shared relations retain the same internal well-foundedness under GBC,
but the available class graphs can change. It is useful to distinguish
absoluteness of the elementary formulas for blocks and recognition
from existence of their class parameters or of the transformations
being considered.

\subsubsection{Formalization and quantitative coding}

\begin{question}[A first verified theorem package]\label{swo:ds:n16.10}
Implement the set-alphabet ordinal spectrum and the
$\mu,\mu+1,\mu+2$ versus later-strata density theorem, then
instantiate them at the small birthday carriers already in ProveIt.
\end{question}
This package would verify both the combinatorial mechanism and its
smallness boundaries without first formalizing arbitrary class models.
The two-point-fiber case is a particularly useful regression target:
counting jumps as disjoint open intervals would produce a false proof.

\begin{question}[Quantitative compatibility of the constructions]\label{swo:ds:n16.11}
Find sharp birthday and support bounds for prefix completion,
termination encodings, and the tree isomorphisms; determine which maps
commute with increasing birthday cutoffs.
\end{question}
Equation~\eqref{swo:ds:eq:centeredbirthday} is explicit, while the global
back-and-forth isomorphisms generally are not birthday-minimal.
Compatibility should mean equality or a specified coherent commuting
diagram of maps, not only the existence of unrelated embeddings at
each stage.
